alex_chung: FYI perf regression on mixtral-7b after the kernel-selector canary. Throughput down ~18% for batched requests >8. P95 tail increased noticeably. Dumping numbers and a trimmed profile below.

maria_gonzalez: oh no — which deploy/commit?

alex_chung: canary commit 9f4c2a7 — selector now prefers `fused_attn` for short-ish sequences based on seq_len histogram. Repro script I used:

```bash
./bench.py --model mixtral-7b --batch 16 --ctx 2048 --profile --warmup 50
```

perf-ci-bot: Benchmark run complete: throughput=420 req/s (baseline 510 req/s), p95 latency 63ms (baseline 42ms), avg tokens/request 120

jamal_singh: Can you paste the kernel/time breakdown? NVTX or the lightweight profile helps. Might be KV-cache churn or kernel padding artifacts.

alex_chung: trimmed profile paste:

```
- selected_kernel: fused_attn
- avg_tokens_per_request: 120
- kernel_time (per token avg): 28ms -> 46ms
- memcpy: 6ms -> 7ms
- kv-cache write spikes at seq rollover (every ~512 tokens)
- observed extra padding per head: +24 bytes/row
```

maria_gonzalez: interesting — `fused_attn` usually helps long contiguous sequences. Mixtral head_dim=128 and kv_dim=4096-ish, so fused path might be suffering if it expects head_dim % 32 == 0 vectorization without extra loop unrolling. Could be padding + cache line effects.

alex_chung: forcing `KERNEL_OVERRIDE=fused_attn` reproduced regression (as expected). Tiling it back to `tiled_attn` returns throughput ~495 req/s and p95 ~45ms, but memory use +4% and max safe batch size drops from 32->24.

jamal_singh: that suggests selector scoring is incomplete. Current score uses just expected latency from seq_len distribution. We should add penalties/considerations for (head_dim, kv_dim, batch_size) and estimated padding overhead. Also KV eviction heuristics: if avg_seq_per_batch < X we get thrash.

alex_chung: also saw RoPE scale artifacts when switching kernels — the attention magnitude distribution shifts and tail spikes. Might interact with quantized kernels too. Qwen and Mixtral both showed similar but different magnitudes.

maria_gonzalez: note: Mixtral vs Llama differences: Mixtral has wider head_dim and denser KV layouts. Tiled kernels sometimes better for small batches because fused kernels pay a fixed setup cost. So batching heuristics must be kernel-aware.

jamal_singh: propose changes: 
- extend kernel selector scoring to include head_dim and kv_dim and batch_size
- add a padding penalty: if head_dim % vector_width != 0 then add penalty
- change batching heuristic: for kernels with high padding overhead, prefer smaller batches or different kernel families
- KV tweak: when avg_seq_per_batch < 40, proactively flush partial blocks to avoid write thrash

alex_chung: can you sketch a simple scoring pseudo-config? I started one:

```yaml
kernel_score:
  base: latency_est_ms
  penalties:
    - condition: head_dim % vector_width != 0
      add_ms: 15
    - condition: batch_size > 8 and kv_dim > 4096
      add_ms: 10
    - condition: avg_seq_per_batch < 40
      add_ms: 8
  weights:
    latency: 1.0
    memory: 0.2
    p95_tail: 0.5
```

maria_gonzalez: looks good as a starting point. We should also expose model_family overrides (e.g., mixtral: prefer tiled for batch>8 unless ctx>1500). Keep it data-driven so we can update from CI sweeps.

alex_chung: I'll run a sweep matrix across models: {Llama-2-13b, Mixtral-7b, Qwen-7b} x batches [1,2,4,8,16,32] x ctx [512,1024,2048] x kernels [fused,tiled,chunked]. Results will be uploaded to CI. Expect ~3-4 hours total.

perf-ci-bot: Created benchmark job #1829 (mixtral-kernel-sweep). ETA ~48m. Artifacts will include per-kernel NVTX, memory traces, and throughput CSV.

maria_gonzalez: prioritize Mixtral and Qwen first (prod signals show tails). If sweep confirms selector mis-rank, we can roll a v2 with model-specific overrides and a runtime flag `runtime.kernel_selector.v2=true` for canary.

jamal_singh: I'll draft the PR for selector changes: add new scoring function, model_family config map, and unit tests asserting expected kernel choice for synthetic inputs. Also include telemetry: why a kernel was chosen (score breakdown) for traceability.

alex_chung: SG. After PR, run A/B on dedicated pool with synthetic warm runs to avoid cold KV OOMs. Also add a synthetic workload that mimics prod sequence distribution (a mix of short chat + long doc).

maria_gonzalez: small operational note: when trying kernels in prod, add a small ramp rule: start at 1% traffic, monitor p95 and OOMs for 30 minutes then 10% then 100%.

alex_chung: agreed. Will post CI artifacts here when job completes; thanks everyone.

(perf-ci-bot) :white_check_mark: job queued/started

infra-bot: HEADS-UP: dedicated-pool-3 has a recent rollout scheduled at 03:00 UTC that might affect canary runs. Recommend running on pool-2 or coordinate with oncall.

alex_chung: noted, will use pool-2.

maria_gonzalez: thanks — ping me when results land, I'll convert promising heuristics into the config map and ship the PR.

jamal_singh: PR draft: https://git.redwood.dev/r/inference/runtime/pulls/512  (WIP)

alex_chung: perfect.

(perf-ci-bot reaction: :thumbsup:)
